# Title page {.unnumbered}

A practical book for R users ready to develop their analysis and delivery skills.

Move from repeated scripts to reusable functions, from a single chart to a report or application that others can use, and from “it runs on my machine” to code that can be tested and traced. These transitions organize the book: technical choices serve a concrete analytical task.

**Author: Jaime Yan** · Online practice edition

[Read the preface](preface.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Choose a reading path](reading-guide.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
[Start the companion lab](companion.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

## Four units, one focus on delivery {.unnumbered}

| Unit | Question you will address | Expected outcome |
|---|---|---|
| [Complex analyses](unit-1-map.qmd) | How do you turn mixed data sources and repeated scripts into a clear, reliable analysis? | Reusable data-processing functions, tables, and plots |
| [Professional deliverables](unit-2-map.qmd) | How do you put results into the hands of the people who need them? | A report, dashboard, or interactive application |
| [Package development](unit-3-map.qmd) | How do you make code maintainable, testable, and shareable? | An R package with documentation and tests |
| [AI and domain applications](unit-4-map.qmd) | How do you evaluate AI assistance and address requirements in specialist settings? | An AI workflow with explicit checks and domain examples |

## Prerequisites {#prerequisites .unnumbered}

You should be able to read a CSV, filter and summarize data, create a basic ggplot, and understand function calls and pipes. With those skills, you can start at the first chapter. Readers in clinical research and pharmaceuticals can also follow the [domain reading path](reading-guide.qmd#clinical-path).

For a refresher, read the Whole game section of [R for Data Science, second edition](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/), then import, tidy, and plot a dataset of your own. You do not need prior experience with package development, Shiny, or LLM APIs.

## Book, practice, and reference library {.unnumbered}

The chapters follow learning outcomes; the [companion lab](companion.qmd) supplies tasks and acceptance criteria; the [conference catalog](https://yanmingyu92.github.io/posit-conf-2026-bilingual/catalog.html) provides access to the original workshops. You can read this book without browsing the catalog first.

posit::conf workshops are an important source. Other books and official documentation provide conceptual support and further reading. Each chapter retains a SOURCES section. See [Further reading](further-reading.qmd) for additional resources and [Authorship and acknowledgments](acknowledgments.qmd) for the distinction between the book author and its source authors.
